answer: Each identity locks 70 in an atlas registry and posts a key-bound commitment with a walnut seal: its action's hash. At the close it reveals it; an auditor's prism check confirms the hash and no conflicting action was signed. Double-signing or copying burns the bond and voids payment. Each fake needs its own 70 bond, 30 fee, and 40 of work, so the k-th fake costs 140 and 1,000 fakes cost 140,000, with nothing shared. A rented commitment fails: its key cannot make the reveal, and duplicate hashes burn the cluster's bonds. An honest agent pays 70 once and recovers its bond on a clean reveal.
